metadata.title: High-Performance Computing Identity and Access

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for ensuring correct identification, authentication, attribution, and authorization of users, workloads, and schedulers in shared high-performance computing environments.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: HPC identity systems, batch schedulers, job submission interfaces, and non-interactive execution contexts.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Governs identity, job attribution, and access control in scheduler-mediated HPC platforms.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: HPC identity and access builds on foundational trust in shared HPC execution platforms.

metadata.remarks: High‑Performance Computing Identity and Access defines the trust properties required to correctly attribute, authorize, and constrain users and workloads in scheduler-driven HPC environments. This pattern explicitly addresses non-interactive job execution, shared login infrastructure, and role separation between users, schedulers, and platform administrators.

components.title: Job Identity Attribution
components.description: Unambiguous attribution of HPC jobs to accountable user or service identities.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Abuse of valid accounts to submit or execute unauthorized HPC jobs.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Binding job execution context to authenticated and attributable identities.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Lifecycle management of user and service identities.
Traceability of job execution to initiating identities.

components.title: Scheduler Access Control
components.description: Restriction and governance of access to scheduler submission and control functions.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Privilege escalation through scheduler or access-control misconfiguration.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Role-based and policy-driven authorization for scheduler operations.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Account and role management for scheduler access.
Least privilege enforced for job submission and control.

components.title: Role Separation and Delegation
components.description: Separation of duties between users, schedulers, and platform administrators.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Privilege escalation through role confusion or excessive delegation.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Explicit separation of user, scheduler, and administrative privileges.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Separation of duties between HPC operational roles.
Restriction on changes to identity and role configuration.
